pages.text: A morning after rain. The paddy bank was still damp.
Dingding took a basket. "I will go down without falling." One patch of earth gleamed smooth.
Grandma led. "My feet know this whole path." She hummed.
Her feet followed the song. One, two, one, two.
Her third step landed. The foot slid far forward.
Grandma landed on her bottom. "Oh dear!"
"This used to be rough." Rain had smoothed the earth.
Dingding looked carefully, avoiding shiny places and choosing only rough ground.
Dingding reached the lower field, leaving one footprint at a time on the bank.
Grandma followed the footprints, all on rough earth. "My song needs a rest today."
